title: Mixed bubbles in a binary mixture of spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates
authors: Uyen Ngoc Le, Ha Phuong Uyen Mai, Hieu Binh Le, Hiroki Saito
abstract: In mean-field theory, the ground state of a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in a uniform system is either uniformly mixed or totally separated. Beyond-mean-field effects introduce an additional phase, the mixed-bubble state, in which the two components remain mixed within one of the separated domains. Here we show that a mixed-bubble state can emerge in a binary mixture of spin-1 ${}^{7}{\rm{Li}}$ and ${}^{23}{\rm{Na}}$ BECs even within the mean-field framework. We further demonstrate the existence of a metastable uniformly-mixed state, which undergoes a transition to the mixed-bubble state triggered by a local perturbation.
summary: This paper investigates the complex phase behavior of a binary mixture of spin-1 BECs, demonstrating the existence of a novel 'mixed-bubble' ground state using mean-field theory. The authors show that the stability of this phase depends critically on the applied magnetic field, offering a pathway to engineer specific spatial mixing patterns in quantum gas systems.
main_problem: To theoretically demonstrate the emergence of a mixed-bubble state in a binary mixture of spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) using mean-field theory.
main_result: The study shows that the mixed-bubble phase exists in the ground state phase diagram, contrasting with simpler predictions, and that a metastable uniformly-mixed state can transition into this mixed-bubble state via local perturbations.
method: The analysis employs mean-field theory, solving coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations and minimizing the total energy/Gibbs free energy to map out the ground state phase diagram.
model_or_system: The system is a binary mixture of spin-1 $^{7}{m{Li}}$ and $^{23}{m{Na}}$ BECs in a uniform trap, governed by mean-field interactions and subject to external magnetic fields.
key_observables: Ground-state phase diagram ($ ar{n}_1$ vs $ ar{n}_2$), density distributions ($ho_j(r)$), magnetization profiles ($\mathbf{F}^{(j)}(r)$), and the Gibbs free energy $g(R)$.
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength ($B_z$), average densities ($ ar{n}_1,  ar{n}_2$), and the mixing ratio ($R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is in the thermodynamic limit, zero total magnetization ($\sum_j \mathbf{f}^{(j)}(r) = 0$), and relies on mean-field approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing three distinct phases (mixed-bubble, uniformly-mixed, totally-separated) as a function of $B_z$, and show density/magnetization profiles characterizing these different spatial domain structures.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using the GP equations, analyzes the energy landscape via the Gibbs free energy $g(R)$ to predict phase stability, and finally uses dynamic arguments to show the transition between the metastable uniform state and the mixed-bubble state.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical mechanism for stabilizing complex, non-trivial spatial structures (mixed bubbles) in spinor BEC mixtures purely through mean-field interactions, which is crucial for designing quantum simulators.

(a) Ground-state phase di- agram with respect to the average densities ¯n1 = N1/V and ¯n2 = N2/V . The circles labeled I-III indicate the parame- ters used in the lower panels. (b) Two-dimensional density distributions obtained by solving the GP equation. (c) One- dimensional density proﬁles nj(x, y = 0) and magnetization proﬁles F (j)(x, y = 0), where the origin is located at the cen- ter. States I, II, and III correspond to the uniformly-mixed, mixed-bubble, and totally-separated phases, respectively.

FIG. 2. Ground-state phases as a function of the external magnetic ﬁeld Bz for ﬁxed average densities ¯n1 = ¯n2 = 2 × 1014 cm−3. Shown are the magnetizations F (j) = |F (j)| and F (j) z of the ground-state domains. In the mixed-bubble phase, 7Li occupies both the mixed and pure-7Li domains, re- sulting in two branches for F (1) and F (1) z . The upper branches terminate at Bz ≃2.36 G, where the pure-7Li domain van- ishes. The insets show representative GP density proﬁles for Bz = 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 G.
